name: Ferrogate Freight Elevator Platform
description: Massive open-air elevator platforms built into the sides of mega-structures and industrial towers, capable of lifting entire vehicles and cargo containers between street level and upper commercial floors. They're slow, loud, and essential — without the Freight Elevators, the upper floors of GLMZ's tower blocks would be unreachable by anything heavier than a person. The platforms have no walls, just safety rails and a prayer. Riding one up forty stories on an open slab of metal with a loaded cargo trike is an experience that never gets comfortable.
cost: Φ5-20 per use depending on weight
common_usage: Moving cargo and vehicles to upper floors, construction material delivery, vertical logistics.
story_hooks: A Freight Elevator descends past the basement level and keeps going — someone has extended the shaft into the Underworld
The elevator operator has been running a clandestine passenger service to floors that don't appear on the building directory
physical_description: A massive steel platform roughly 20×30 feet, supported by thick hydraulic columns and anchored to weathered concrete. Rust blooms through chipped industrial-gray paint, and safety rails—dented from decades of cargo impacts—run along three sides, their yellow warning stripes faded to sickly mustard. Hydraulic hoses thick as fire hoses snake across the platform's underside, weeping fluid onto the corroded deck below.
